old_title: Where to find the best PS5 Black Friday deals on games, consoles and more
new_title: I've found the best PS5 Black Friday deals available now, including GTA 6 bundles
old_text:
If you're looking for the best PS5 Black Friday deals, it's here that I'm keeping an eye out for the top offers. While PlayStation Direct's Black Friday offers are live, with discounts on everything from DualSense controllers and gaming headsets to PlayStation Plus subscriptions, there's still no sign of a price cut on the PS5 console itself.
That's particularly disappointing given the PS5's price increase earlier this year, which has made the console more expensive than ever. Stock is another issue, with the PS5 Pro currently sold out at several retailers. Still, there are ways to save if you're hoping to pick up a PlayStation this Black Friday.
While standalone console discounts are proving hard to come by, I've found some bundles that could work out cheaper than buying everything separately. These include PS5 packages with additional controllers and games, such as the new GTA 6, so they're worth considering if you're after more than just the console.
I'll be tracking PS5 prices throughout the Black Friday sales, keeping an eye out for new console discounts, refurbished offers and savings on games and accessories. I'll update this guide as the best PS5 Black Friday deals land, so keep checking back for the latest offers worth your money.
Best PS5 Black Friday 2026 deals:
- Best console deal: PS5 Slim (refurbished): Was £520, now £429.99, Playstation.com
- Best VR deal: PlayStation VR2 with 'Horizon Call of The Mountain': Was £399.99, now £309.99, Playstation.com
- Best controller deal: PlayStation 5 DualSense controller: Was £64.99, now £42.99, Amazon.co.uk
Deals picked by Alex Lee
I've been covering Black Friday for more than a decade, so I know a good deal when I see one. I've been tracking the price of the PS5 since it launched in 2020, when I kicked off The Independent's live stock tracker during the 'Great PS5 Stock Shortage'. Having followed the console's price over the past six years, I know just how low it can go, and I'll be keeping a close eye on retailers to bring you the best PS5 deals this Black Friday.
Best PS5 Black Friday deals
Of all the early bundle deals I've seen so far, this one from Smyths is among the best. In the deal, you get a PlayStation 5 slim disc console with 1TB of storage, as well as Marvel's Wolverine game, which was released in September this year. In his review of Marvel's Wolverine, gaming correspondent Jake Brigstock awarded it four out of five stars and said that it delivered all the "gory, gritty and relentless combat" promised. The game usually costs about £70 but this bundle means you'll get it for about £30 on top of the PS5's usual price.
Sony's PS VR2 turns the PlayStation 5 into a full-blown virtual-reality console, complete with exclusives such as Horizon Call of the Mountain and VR modes for Gran Turismo 7 and No Man's Sky. In his review, Steve Hogarty described it as one of the "best and easiest headsets to set up and use". Right now, you can save £90 on this Horizon Call of the Mountain bundle at PlayStation Direct.
If you've already got a PS5 and are looking for a second (or third) controller, Amazon and Smyths Toys has slashed more than £20 off the rarely ever discounted DualSense gamepad for Black Friday - that's cheaper than Argos's, PlayStation Direct's and Currys's Black Friday prices.
One of the best accessories you can own, it features incredible haptic feedback that brings games to life, and if you like to play couch co-op with your buddies, you'll need more than one. The original white, midnight black, cosmic red, starlight blue, nova pink and galactic purple colourways can all be picked up for £42.99.
If you fancy something a little more exciting than the standard DualSense controller colourways, then PlayStation Direct has also slashed £20 off its limited-edition designs for Black Friday. You can choose from limited-edition Ghost of Yōtei, God of War, Death Stranding 2, 007 First Light, Marathon, Marvel's Wolverine controllers and more.
They all feature the same haptic feedback and adaptive triggers as the standard DualSense, but with designs that celebrate PlayStation's biggest titles. All have been reduced to £54.99.
The DualSense Edge is Sony's pro-level controller designed with the needs of esports players in mind. The premium pad lets you tweak things to suit your playstyle, remapping controls, instantly switching between gaming profiles, and adjust trigger sensitivities and thumbstick dead zones.
As a niche product, it's appropriately pricey but now the DualSense Edge is on sale at Argos.
Designed to connect seamlessly using Sony's proprietary PlayStation Link protocol, the Pulse Elite gaming headset delivers lossless 3D audio, studio-grade sound quality courtesy of Audeze, an AI-powered noise-cancelling boom mic and multi-point connectivity for switching between the PS5, the PlayStation Portal or any Bluetooth-capable device. It's now reduced to just £89.99 in PlayStation's Black Friday sale, with Amazon and Currys price-matching.
Several retailers have cut the price of Sony's PS5 pulse explore wireless earbuds for Black Friday, but Argos is currently the cheapest option with stock available. Compatible with the PS5 console family and PC, these earbuds were originally priced at £154.99, but are now available from Argos for £119.99. Noise cancelling and with an integrated microphone, these wireless earbuds charge by USB and promise up to 15 hours of battery life.
Sony's customisable access controller has been slashed by £31.50 in Amazon's Black Friday sale, which is the best deal we've seen so far. Making gaming more accessible for players with disabilities, the circular controller features interchangeable buttons and stick caps, adjustable layout, giving you the ability to create custom control profiles.
Sony has slashed 33 per cent off a 12-month Premium membership for Black Friday, taking the price down to £80.39. The top-tier subscription provides access to hundreds of games in PlayStation's game catalogue, a library of classic PlayStation titles, game trials and cloud streaming, as well as online multiplayer and a rolling stream of new monthly games. That's a £39.60 saving. The subscription automatically renews at £119.99 after the first year unless cancelled.
If you're yet to upgrade to the PS5, this bundle includes the 825GB digital edition console, GTA 6 and an additional DualSense Edge wireless controller. The latter is Sony's premium controller, with customisable controls, adjustable triggers and replaceable stick modules,
In timing with the new James Bond announcement, this limited-edition DualSense wireless controller, inspired by 007 First Light is reduced in EE's Black Friday sale. It features a striking gold finish and gun-barrel detailing, alongside the usual DualSense features, including haptic feedback and adaptive triggers for a more immersive gaming experience.
Best Black Friday deals on PS5 games
Yet to play the latest game in EA's footballing franchise? You can currently save 50 per cent on FC 27 at the PlayStation Store for Black Friday. "EA Sports FC 27 is a solid football video game. It has a brand new mode in The Grounds, along with meaningful tweaks to the transfer system in career mode, and gameplay tweaks," said gaming correspondent Jake Brigstock in his EA Sports FC 27 review.
One of the biggest PS5 exclusives of 2026 has already had its price slashed for Black Friday, less than two months after launch. Developed by Insomniac Games, the studio behind Marvel's Spider-Man, Marvel's Wolverine puts you in the claws of the iconic X-Men character. "Marvel's Wolverine is a great fast-paced, action-heavy linear superhero game that fulfils the Wolverine fantasy incredibly well," gaming correspondent Jake Brigstock wrote in his Marvel Wolverine's review.
The disc edition for PS5 has had its price cut by Amazon from £69.99 to £39.94 - a 43 per cent discount.
When will PS5 Black Friday deals begin in 2026?
Sony's Black Friday sale officially kicked off on Monday 16 November, with discounts on PS5 peripherals, accessories, PlayStation Plus memberships and more. You can save £20 on DualSense controllers, £30 on the DualSense Edge and access controllers, as well as £40 on the Pulse Elite headset. The sale runs until 30 November.
You can also save up to £90 on selected collector's editions and up to 33 per cent on PlayStation Plus memberships.
If you're looking for games, Sony kicked off its PlayStation Store Black Friday sale on 4 November, with discounts of up to 75 per cent on thousands of PS5, PS4 and PS VR2 games, expansions and DLC.
Sadly, there are no discounts on the PS5 or PS5 Pro consoles at PlayStation Direct just yet, but I'll be watching for any savings as Black Friday approaches.
Why you can't buy a PlayStation 5 Pro
In April 2026, Sony hiked the price of all three PS5 consoles by a whopping £90, blaming global RAM shortages and higher manufacturing costs due to global tariffs. The PS5 Slim with the disc drive increased to £569.99, the PS5 Slim digital edition rose to £519.99, and the PS5 Pro went from £699.99 to an eye-watering £789.99. The latter is also out of stock everywhere.
When it comes to shopping for PS5 deals in the Black Friday sales this year, there are some small savings on PS5 bundles, but the PS5 Pro remains completely sold out, thanks to RAMageddon and increased demand due to the launch of GTA 6.
The cheapest way to play 'GTA 6'
As The Independent's gaming correspondent, Jake Brigstock, explained in his GTA 6 article, there are two versions of the game available to buy: the Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition. "Basically, the Ultimate Edition allows access to more shops, vehicles, weapons, and garages," wrote Jake. "However, none of this is truly essential to get the most out of GTA 6." While the Ultimate Edition will set you back £89.99 (Playstation.com), the Standard Edition is £20 cheaper, at £69.99 (Playstation.com).
Jake's advice is: "If you want to enjoy GTA 6's story, explore, and complete activities without being too fussed about customising Jason and Lucia's appearance, then the Standard Edition is the best bet." He added that, even if you do opt for the Ultimate Edition, "a lot of the upgrades unlock as you play through the story. In other words, not all of this extra content is accessible from the very beginning."
If you're treating yourself to a new console at the same time as buying the game, it's also worth keeping an eye out for bundle offers (such as those listed above), which can save you money compared with buying a new console and GTA 6 separately.
